dek: You've updated your CV and kept applying. Still nothing. Let's check where your search might be getting stuck and what you can try next.
imageAlt: Person typing on a laptop at a wooden desk, with a cup of coffee and an open notebook beside them

leadMagnet.title: Want a quick check before your next application goes out?
leadMagnet.body: Use the ATS CV Checklist to catch formatting problems, missing details and other avoidable mistakes before you press send.
leadMagnet.afterHeading: Check the boring things before changing everything

dek: The extra responsibility is already yours. Here's how to prepare a clear conversation about the role, recognition and next steps you're asking for.
imageAlt: Two colleagues talking across a table in a bright office, with a notebook open between them

leadMagnet.title: Does the way people see your work match the role you want?
leadMagnet.body: Take the Personal Brand Audit before your conversation to check whether your contribution is visible to the people making the decision.
leadMagnet.afterHeading: Build a case you can fit on one page

dek: Start with one person and a question you genuinely want answered. Practical messages and follow-ups for building professional connections without the awkward pitch.
imageAlt: Laptop showing a LinkedIn profile on a wooden desk beside a coffee mug and a pot plant

leadMagnet.title: Will your headline make sense when they look you up?
leadMagnet.body: Download before-and-after LinkedIn headline rewrites and a simple formula for describing the work you do and the work you want.
leadMagnet.afterHeading: Be clear enough for someone to help

dek: You want different work, but you have a life to support. Explore your options, understand what transfers and test a direction before making a big move.
imageAlt: Woman in a grey blazer sitting at a desk beside a laptop, looking away in thought

leadMagnet.title: Not sure whether it is the work or the circumstances?
leadMagnet.body: The 5-Minute Career Diagnostic helps you name what is keeping you stuck before you start researching a new direction.
leadMagnet.afterHeading: Work out what you actually want to change

dek: You don't need forty perfect answers. Prepare real examples, practise saying them aloud and arrive knowing what you want to ask too.
imageAlt: Two colleagues talking across a table in a bright office, with a notebook open between them

dek: A clear opening answer helps the interviewer understand your experience. Build yours with examples for graduates, experienced candidates and career changers.
imageAlt: Woman in a grey blazer sitting at a desk beside a laptop, looking away in thought

dek: The salary question doesn't have to become a guessing game. Prepare a researched range, understand the package and find words you're comfortable saying.
imageAlt: Person typing on a laptop at a wooden desk, with a cup of coffee and an open notebook beside them

dek: Before you pay for another certificate, check what you'll learn, what it costs and how you'll use it. Choose a course that supports the work you want to do.
imageAlt: Laptop showing a LinkedIn profile on a wooden desk beside a coffee mug and a pot plant
